opportunities.title: Training Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society can apply, as long as you are studying or working in the UK, or the course you wish to attend is being held in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become Society members; others should be a Society member for at least one year.
opportunities.summary: Grants of up to £1,200 to enable members to attend formal short training courses or a collaborative visit to another laboratory to train in specific genetic/genomic techniques.

opportunities.title: Junior Scientist Conference Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Undergraduate, Master’s and PhD student members and postdoctoral members within six years of their PhD viva for Scheme A; PhD students and postdoctoral members within six years of their PhD viva for Schemes B & C. Applicants must be UK‑based (or UK‑based for overseas conferences) and must present a poster or talk.
opportunities.summary: Supports attendance at Genetics Society meetings, SIG meetings, or other genetics‑related conferences (including virtual). Grants range from up to £200 for Society meetings, up to £500 (or £750 for Adelphi co‑sponsored) for other conferences, and up to £300 for virtual conference registration.

opportunities.title: Public Engagement Grant
opportunities.summary: Grants of up to £1,000 to support public engagement activities related to genetics, covering travel and materials costs (UK‑based travel only).

opportunities.title: Heredity Fieldwork Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society can apply, provided they are studying or working in the UK, or intend to carry out fieldwork in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others need at least one year of membership.
opportunities.summary: Awards up to £2,000 (usually below £1,700) to cover travel, accommodation, subsistence and consumables for field‑based genetic research projects suitable for publication in the journal Heredity.
